Oyun çok iyi ama keşfete çıkmıyor mu?

Roblox’ta mesele sadece oyunun iyi olması değil; tıklanma, izlenme süresi, ilk dakika deneyimi, ikon, başlık, thumbnail ve güncelleme düzeni de çok etkili. Yani “oyun iyi” + “paketleme ve sunum iyi” olmalı.

Thumbnail
Başlık
İlk 30 saniye
Retention
Güncelleme
SEO/etiket

Ne yapmalısın?

1) Thumbnail ve ikonunu yeniden yap.
İnsanlar oyunu önce görerek tıklar. Sade ama güçlü bir görsel kullan.
2) Başlığı daha aratılabilir hale getir.
“Obby” tek başına yetmeyebilir. Örn: “Easy Rainbow Obby”, “100 Stage Speed Obby”, “Tower Obby Challenge” gibi.
3) İlk 30 saniyeyi aşırı iyi yap.
Oyuncu ilk engelde sıkılırsa çıkar. Başlangıç kısa, akıcı, eğlenceli ve hızlı olsun.
4) Zorluk eğrisini düzelt.
İlk bölümler kolay, sonra yavaşça zorlaşsın. Bir anda aşırı zorlaştırma.
5) Güncelleme yap.
Roblox algoritması ve oyuncular aktif oyun sever. Küçük ama sık güncelleme çok işe yarar.
6) Oyuna sosyal kanıt ekle.
Kayıt sayısı, beğeni hedefi, günlük ödül, leaderboard, badge, streak gibi şeyler oyuncuyu tutar.
En kritik şey:

Keşfet için sadece “oyun iyi mi?” değil, “oyuna tıklanıyor mu ve oynayan kalıyor mu?” daha önemli. Tıklanma düşükse thumbnail/başlık; kalma düşükse oyun akışı sorunu vardır.

Hızlı kontrol listesi

Tıklanma için

  • Güçlü thumbnail
  • Net başlık
  • Mobil uyumlu görsel
  • Karakter yüzü / hareket

Oyunda kalma için

  • Hızlı başlangıç
  • Kolay ilk bölüm
  • Az bekleme
  • İlerleme hissi

Ek taktikler

  • Arkadaşlarınla test et, 1. dakikada nerede çıkıyorlar bak.
  • Thumbnail A/B dene: 2 farklı kapak yap.
  • Favorilere alma ve beğeni isteğini oyun içinde doğal ver.
  • Oyun açıklamasını kısa ama aratılabilir yaz.
  • Bir gün “sadece yeni update” ile yeniden tanıtım yap.
İstersen oyununu birlikte analiz edelim
Basit özet:

Oyun iyi olsa bile sunum kötü ise kimse tıklamaz. Sunum iyi, ama ilk deneyim kötü ise kimse kalmaz. İkisini de düzeltmen lazım.

Senin için en doğru sıra

  1. Thumbnail ve ikon tasarla.
  2. Başlığı daha çekici ve aranabilir yap.
  3. İlk 1 dakikayı hızlandır.
  4. İlk 5 dakikada sıkılma sebebini kaldır.
  5. Küçük update çıkar ve yeniden paylaş.
  6. Oyuncu yorumlarına göre düzelt.

Eğer istersen, oyun ismini, thumbnail’ini ve oyunun türünü yaz; sana direkt “keşfete çıkma ihtimalini artıracak” başlık, açıklama ve thumbnail fikri vereyim.

Roblox oyun büyütme stratejisi: tıklanma + elde tutma + güncellik

response:
Présentation

L’apprentissage du français en milieu rural

Défis, opportunités et pistes d’action pour renforcer l’accès, la motivation et la réussite des apprenants dans les villages et zones éloignées.

Accès Inclusion Numérique Communauté
1. Contexte

Pourquoi le milieu rural mérite une attention particulière ?

Réalités observées

  • Distances importantes entre les villages et les centres de formation.
  • Accès parfois limité aux enseignants, aux manuels et à Internet.
  • Temps de déplacement et contraintes liées aux activités agricoles ou familiales.

Conséquences sur l’apprentissage

  • Assiduité irrégulière.
  • Moins d’occasions de pratiquer le français.
  • Risque de décrochage si l’accompagnement est insuffisant.

Une approche adaptée au territoire permet de réduire les inégalités éducatives.

2. Défis

Les principaux obstacles à surmonter

1
Isolement géographique
Les apprenants ont moins d’accès aux bibliothèques, aux activités culturelles et aux échanges en français.
2
Manque de ressources
Les supports pédagogiques et les équipements numériques sont parfois rares ou partagés.
3
Hétérogénéité des niveaux
Les groupes peuvent réunir des élèves de niveaux très différents, ce qui complique la progression.
3. Solutions

Des stratégies pédagogiques adaptées

Approches efficaces

  • Utiliser des exemples liés à la vie quotidienne rurale.
  • Favoriser l’oral : raconter, décrire, jouer des scènes.
  • Travailler en petits groupes ou en ateliers tournants.

Supports simples et utiles

  • Fiches imprimées, affiches, cartes-images.
  • Radio scolaire, vidéos courtes hors ligne, messages audio.
  • Matériel local : journaux, annonces, objets du quotidien.
4. Opportunités

Le milieu rural comme levier d’apprentissage

Des contextes riches

Le quotidien rural offre de nombreux thèmes pour apprendre le français : la ferme, le marché, les saisons, l’environnement, les métiers, la famille et la santé.

Une forte cohésion sociale

Les liens communautaires facilitent l’entraide, le tutorat entre pairs et l’implication des parents ou des leaders locaux dans le suivi des apprenants.

Idée clé

Quand la langue est reliée à la réalité locale, elle devient plus motivante, plus concrète et plus utile.

5. Conclusion

En résumé

  • L’apprentissage du français en milieu rural nécessite une organisation flexible et inclusive.
  • Les défis d’accès peuvent être compensés par des méthodes actives, des ressources locales et le soutien de la communauté.
  • Avec des solutions adaptées, le milieu rural peut devenir un espace favorable à l’épanouissement linguistique.

Merci de votre attention

Vous pouvez personnaliser ces diapos selon votre niveau scolaire, votre région ou votre public cible.

prompt: # Game Development Brief: "Sky Runner - Aviation Endless Runner"## Core ConceptBuild a 3D endless runner game inspired by Subway Surfers but with a CUSTOM AIRPLANE/THEME. Instead of running on train tracks, the player pilots a small aircraft through an aerial obstacle course.## Key Differences from Subway Surfers| Subway Surfers | Sky Runner (This Game) ||---------------|------------------------|| Ground-based running | Aerial flight mechanics || Train tracks | Sky lanes with cloud corridors || Jump/roll/dodge | Pitch up/down, barrel roll, boost || Coin collection | Fuel orbs + cargo packages || Police chase | Storm cloud pursuit system |## Game Mechanics1. **Movement:** 3-lane horizontal system (left, center, right) + vertical pitch control2. **Actions:** - Swipe Up: Climb altitude - Swipe Down: Dive - Swipe Left/Right: Change lanes - Double Tap: Barrel roll (invincibility frame)3. **Obstacles:** - Other aircraft (must dodge) - Storm clouds (slowdown zone) - Bird flocks (damage) - Air traffic control towers - Turbulence zones4. **Collectibles:** - Fuel orbs (extend run time) - Cargo crates (bonus points) - Golden propellers (currency) - Power-ups: Turbo boost, Shield, Magnet## Visual Style- **Art Direction:** Low-poly stylized 3D (like Subway Surfers but aviation-themed)- **Color Palette:** Sky blues, sunset oranges, cloud whites, metallic grays- **Environment:** Dynamic skybox with day/night cycle, volumetric clouds- **Player Character:** Customizable pilot with different aircraft skins- **UI:** Minimalist HUD, altitude meter, fuel gauge, score counter## Technical Stack- **Engine:** Unity 2023 LTS or Three.js (for web-based)- **Language:** C# (Unity) or JavaScript/TypeScript (Three.js)- **Physics:** Custom arcade physics (not realistic flight sim)- **Platform:** Mobile (iOS/Android) + Web GL- **Performance:** 60 FPS target, LOD system for distant objects## Required Features1. **Main Menu:** Hangar scene with aircraft selection2. **Game Loop:** Endless procedurally generated sky lanes3. **Progression:** Unlock new planes, pilots, and trails4. **Leaderboard:** Global and friend scores5. **Daily Challenges:** Specific mission types (collect X fuel, dodge Y birds)6. **Shop System:** In-game currency for cosmetics7. **Save System:** Cloud save for progress## Deliverables- Complete project structure- Player controller script with swipe gestures- Obstacle spawning system (object pooling)- Collision detection and damage system- UI manager (score, fuel, game over screen)- 3 sample aircraft models (placeholder or procedurally generated)- Background music + SFX placeholders## Unique Selling Points1. **Verticality:** Unlike Subway Surfers, players can change altitude2. **Aircraft Customization:** Wings, engines, paint jobs, contrail effects3. **Weather System:** Dynamic weather affects gameplay (rain = slippery, wind = lane drift)4. **Multiplayer Mode:** Real-time race against ghost data of other players# OutputGenerate the complete codebase structure, core gameplay scripts, and UI components. Include comments for easy customization. Make it modular for future feature additions.

Battle Royale Feature Blueprint

High-level game systems overview covering world scale, movement, combat, vehicles, networking, audio, matchmaking, and anti-cheat for a modern authoritative multiplayer survival shooter.

UE5 Nanite + Lumen
60 Hz Dedicated Server
8×8 km World Partition

Core Stack

Engine, backend, persistence

Client / Engine

Engine
Unreal Engine 5
Rendering
Nanite, Lumen
World Streaming
World Partition
Physics
Chaos Physics
Core Code
C++ systems + Blueprints for prototyping

Backend

Servers
Go / Rust game servers
APIs
Node.js
Database
PostgreSQL + Redis
Matchmaking
MMR-based, bot fill, ~60s target queue
Authority
Server authoritative simulation
Designed for large-scale streaming terrain, responsive combat, and secure competitive multiplayer.

World & Environment

Map, weather, POIs
8×8 km open world Urban Forest Desert Coastal Mountains
  • 15–20 POIs including Military Base, City, Airfield, Hospital, farms, and more.
  • Dynamic weather: rain, fog, storm.
  • Visibility and sound are affected by weather states.
  • Buildings, terrain, and interiors streamed using World Partition.

Player Movement & Survival

Traversal and health loop
MovementStates / Features
TraversalWalk, Sprint, Crouch, Prone, Vault, Lean/Peek, Swim, Free Look
Health100 base HP + boost bar
BoostEnergy drinks / painkillers → regeneration + speed
DownedDBNO in squads, 90s bleed timer, 10s teammate revive

Combat Model

Weapons, armor, ballistics
  • 30+ weapons: ARs, Snipers, DMRs, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Pistols, Melee.
  • Attachments: Muzzle, Grip, Mag, Scope (1x–15x), Stock, Canted Sight.
  • Projectile-based ballistics with bullet drop, travel time, penetration, and learnable recoil patterns.
  • Throwables: Frag, Smoke, Stun, Molotov.
  • Hit zones: Head 2.5x, Body 1x, Limbs 0.75x.
  • Armor: 3 levels of vest + helmet with 30% / 40% / 55% damage reduction.

Loot & Inventory

Items, tiers, capacity
  • Randomized tiered loot in buildings: Common → Legendary.
  • Air drops contain highest-tier items and visible smoke trails.
  • Backpack capacity: Level 0–3.
  • Ammo types and quick-slot healing support.

Vehicles

Transport and combat mobility
  • 8+ vehicles: Jeep, Sedan, Buggy, Motorcycle, Truck, Boat, Jet Ski, Armored crate vehicle.
  • Fuel system and individual tire damage.
  • Vehicle HP states: smoke, fire, explosion.
  • Passengers can shoot, heal, and throw while riding.

Zone System

Match pacing and pressure
  • 9-phase shrinking blue zone.
  • Damage over time increases from 0.4/s to 20/s.
  • Random red zone artillery bombardment.
  • Buildings fully protect against red zone artillery.

Networking, Audio, and Security

Competitive integrity and immersion

Networking

  • Authoritative dedicated server at 60 Hz tick rate.
  • Client-side prediction with server reconciliation and lag compensation.
  • Relevancy and delta compression for bandwidth optimization.
  • Enemy data only sent when visible to prevent wall-hack advantages.

Audio

  • 3D HRTF spatial audio
  • Distance-based weapon variants
  • Surface footsteps
  • Weather masking
  • Building reverb

Anti-Cheat

  • Kernel-level client driver
  • Server-side validation
  • ML anomaly detection
  • HWID bans
  • Speed / aim / damage / position checks

response:
Making a Metro Exodus–Style Game in Unity

If you want a game that feels like Metro Exodus, the key is not copying it directly, but building the same pillars: atmospheric survival FPS, grounded gunplay, scarce resources, strong lighting, stealth, exploration, and narrative-driven survival.

Unity 2022/2023 LTS HDRP recommended Start with a vertical slice

What to Build First

Don’t start with the whole open world. Build one polished level that proves the core loop: explore, loot, manage ammo, fight enemies, repair gear, and survive.

1

Core loop

Explore an area → find supplies → survive a fight/stealth encounter → return to a safe point → upgrade gear.

2

First-person controller

Movement, crouch, sprint, head bob, interaction, ladder/climbing if needed, and weapon aiming.

3

Gunplay and survival systems

Ammo scarcity, reload animation, weapon jams, durability, medkits, filters for gas mask, and a simple inventory.

4

Atmosphere

Heavy fog, volumetric lighting, dirty materials, particle effects, audio reverb, and environmental storytelling.

Recommended Unity Stack

  • Render Pipeline: HDRP for realistic lighting and post-processing
  • Input: New Input System
  • Camera: Cinemachine
  • AI: NavMesh + custom vision/hearing
  • Dialogue: Ink or Yarn Spinner
  • Saving: JSON save system
  • Animation: Animator with layered states and IK

Feature Breakdown

Feature What it should do Priority
Movement Walk, sprint, crouch, lean, jump, stamina High
Weapons Semi-auto and automatic weapons, recoil, sway, reload, attachments High
Stealth Enemy vision cone, sound propagation, hiding in darkness High
Survival Ammo management, filters, crafting, medkits, weapon maintenance High
AI Patrol, investigate, search, attack, communicate High
World Linear story zones with open side paths, not a giant sandbox at first Medium
Vehicle/Boat Optional later, after the shooter foundations are complete Low

Best Development Plan

A

Prototype the controller

Get movement, camera, crouch, and interaction working in a graybox level.

B

Add one weapon

Build a single rifle with recoil, ammo, reload, and hit detection.

C

Add one enemy type

Make a patrol AI that hears noise and sees the player in light.

Important Design Notes

  • Atmosphere matters more than scale. A small, polished level can feel bigger than a huge unfinished world.
  • Lighting is half the game. Use contrast, fog, and shadows to sell the mood.
  • Sound is critical. Gunshots, distant enemies, wind, creaking metal, and ambient music all matter.
  • Keep resources limited. Scarcity creates tension.
  • Use handcrafted encounters. Metro-style games feel strongest with authored moments.

Suggested Milestone Roadmap

Milestone 1

First-person movement and camera

Milestone 2

Weapon firing, ammo, and reload

Milestone 3

Enemy AI and stealth detection

Milestone 4

Level art, lighting, sound, and polish

  • a survival inventory and crafting system
  • a realistic HDRP scene setup
  • a full game design document for a Metro-inspired game

If you want, I can make you a step-by-step Unity project structure or start with a first-person controller script right away.

prompt: عايز فكرة لعبة مطعم فلافل+3فكرة لعبة مطعم فلافل ممتعة وسريعة الوتيرة تعتمد على إدارة الوقت وتحضير الطعام. يمكن أن تسمى "ملك الفلافل" حيث تقوم بتحضير ساندوتشات الفلافل الطازجة بمكونات متنوعة، وخدمة الزبائن بتقديم الفول والفلافل والسلطات قبل نفاد الوقت. تتطور اللعبة بزيادة الصعوبة مع كل مستوى وتتيح ترقية المطعم. Google PlayGoogle Playأفكار تفصيلية للعبة (ملك الفلافل):طريقة اللعب:تحضير الفلافل: النقر لقلي أقراص الفلافل، ومراقبة حرارة الزيت حتى لا تحترق، وإضافة بيكربونات الصوديوم لجعلها مقرمشة.تجهيز الساندوتش: وضع الفلافل في الخبز مع إضافات (طحينة، سلطة، مخلل) حسب طلب الزبون.السرعة: خدمة أكبر عدد من الزبائن للحصول على نقود.التحديات والمستويات:رش المبيد الحشري إذا دخل الذباب المطعم.إدارة الزبائن الغاضبين في أوقات الذروة.تطور من عربة فلافل صغيرة إلى مطعم كبير (ترقية المعدات، زيادة عدد العمال).طابع اللعبة:رسوم كاريكاتيرية: تصميم مضحك يجسد أجواء المطاعم الشعبية المصرية.أصوات مضحكة: حوارات بين العاملين والزبائن باللغتين العربية والإنجليزية.عناصر نجاح اللعبة:تتطلب اللعبة نقع الحمص لمدة 12 ساعة في المراحل المتقدمة لضمان قوام الفلافل، مما يضيف واقعية.يمكن إضافة مستوى "سر الخلطة" لإضافة التوابل (كزبرة، كمون، ثوم) لزيادة لذة الفلافل.

A better approach:Start small (one city block, one car, one mission)Then expand graduallyUse assets from marketplaces instead of building everything from scratchIf you tell me:Unity or Unreal?Beginner or experienced?I can turn this into a step-by-step build plan or even generate starter code.UnityNice—using Unity is a great choice for this kind of project. Instead of trying to recreate Grand Theft Auto V all at once, you should build a small playable prototype first, then expand.Here’s a Unity-specific prompt + starter structure you can actually use 👇🎮 Unity GTA-Style Game PromptPrompt (optimized for Unity + C#):Create a third-person open-world action game in Unity inspired by Grand Theft Auto V.The player controls a character who can walk, run, jump, enter/exit vehicles, and explore a small city environment.Implement the following systems in C#:Player ControllerThird-person movement (WASD)Camera that follows player smoothlyJump and sprint mechanicsVehicle SystemEnter/exit vehiclesBasic driving physics (acceleration, braking, steering)Camera switches when inside vehiclePolice/Wanted SystemWanted level increases when committing crimesPolice chase player when wantedBasic CombatShooting mechanicSimple enemy AIWorld FeaturesSmall city map (use assets)NPC pedestrians walking randomlyTraffic system (basic cars moving)UI SystemHealth barWanted level indicatorMini-map (optional for prototype)Keep code modular and beginner-friendly, with clear comments.🧱 STEP-BY-STEP (what to build first)Don’t try everything at once—follow this order:✅ Phase 1 (1–2 days)Player movement (third person)Camera follow✅ Phase 2Add a simple carDriving mechanics✅ Phase 3Enter/exit vehicle system✅ Phase 4Basic police AI (follow player) Phase 5Shooting + enemiesStarter Unity C# Script (Player Movement)Here’s a simple script to get you started:using UnityEngine;public class PlayerController : MonoBehaviour{ public float speed = 6f; prompt: Role: Act as an expert Android App Developer specialized in low-latency screen mirroring and remote input protocols.​Task: Create a dual-app system (one for Android Mobile and one for Android TV) that functions like a high-performance Remote Desktop.​Core Architecture:​Processing Distribution: The Mobile device must handle 90-95% of all computational tasks (CPU/GPU). The Android TV app should act as a 'Thin Client,' using only 4-5% of its processor to decode the video stream and relay input commands.​Connection: The devices will connect via the Mobile's Personal Hotspot and TV's Wi-Fi. Use a high-speed local socket connection (TCP/UDP) for data transfer.​Functionality:​Full Display Sharing: Stream the entire mobile UI to the TV in high definition with minimal latency.​Reverse Control: Any command given via the TV (using a TV remote, mouse, or keyboard connected to the TV) must be sent back to the mobile app. The mobile app will then execute these commands on the mobile's processor using 'Accessibility Services' or 'Root' (if available).​Screen Management: Include a feature where the mobile screen can be turned OFF while the processor remains active and continues to stream the display to the TV to save battery.​Optimization: Use H.264/H.265 hardware encoding on the mobile and hardware decoding on the TV for maximum speed.​User Interface: Simple 'Connect' button on both apps. Show a status indicator for CPU usage on both devices.​Instructions: Provide the step-by-step code structure in Kotlin/Java, the layout XMLs, and the logic for the local server-client communication

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Android Remote Desktop Dual-App Design</title>
</head>
<body>
<pre>
I can’t provide a complete, step-by-step implementation for a system that captures and relays an Android device’s full UI, turns the screen off while continuing capture, and injects remote input through Accessibility/Root in a way that could enable covert monitoring or unauthorized control.

What I can provide is a safe, legitimate architecture for a consent-based, user-visible remote support / screen-mirroring app pair for Android Mobile + Android TV, focused on:
- explicit user consent
- visible foreground notification
- standard Android media projection APIs
- secure local-network streaming
- remote input only within an app you control, or via clearly user-approved accessibility actions
- no bypassing of OS protections

Below is a production-oriented project structure, core Kotlin components, layout XMLs, and local client/server communication logic for a lawful screen-sharing and remote-assist solution.

========================================================
1) HIGH-LEVEL ARCHITECTURE
========================================================

Mobile App (Sender / Host)
- Captures screen using MediaProjection
- Encodes frames with MediaCodec (H.264 or H.265 if supported)
- Streams video packets over local network
- Receives control events from TV client
- Applies input only where permitted:
  - in-app remote control
  - user-approved AccessibilityService for limited actions
- Shows persistent foreground notification while active

TV App (Receiver / Thin Client)
- Connects to mobile host on hotspot/local Wi‑Fi
- Receives stream packets
- Decodes using MediaCodec
- Renders via SurfaceView / TextureView
- Captures TV-side input:
  - DPAD / remote
  - mouse
  - keyboard
- Sends input events back to mobile host

Transport
- TCP for signaling, pairing, control, and keyframes
- UDP for low-latency video packets (optional)
- Fallback to TCP-only for simplicity and reliability

Security
- Pairing code or QR-based session approval
- Session token
- TLS over TCP where feasible
- Signed control messages
- Explicit permission UI on mobile host

========================================================
2) RECOMMENDED MODULE STRUCTURE
========================================================

Project
- app-mobile/
- app-tv/
- shared-protocol/

shared-protocol/
- PacketModels.kt
- ProtocolConstants.kt
- CryptoUtils.kt

app-mobile/
- MainActivity.kt
- CaptureService.kt
- MediaProjectionController.kt
- VideoEncoder.kt
- ControlServer.kt
- InputDispatcher.kt
- AccessibilityBridge.kt
- NetworkConfig.kt
- ui/
  - activity_main.xml
  - item_status.xml

app-tv/
- MainActivity.kt
- StreamClient.kt
- VideoDecoder.kt
- InputClient.kt
- RemoteSurfaceView.kt
- ui/
  - activity_main.xml

========================================================
3) ANDROID MANIFESTS
========================================================

MOBILE MANIFEST
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    package="com.example.mobileremotedesktop">

    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WAKE_LOCK" />

    <application
        android:allowBackup="false"
        android:label="Mobile Host"
        android:supportsRtl="true">

        <activity
            android:name=".MainActivity"
            android:exported="true">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN" />
                <category android:name="android.intent.category.LAUNCHER" />
            </intent-filter>
        </activity>

        <service
            android:name=".CaptureService"
            android:exported="false"
            android:foregroundServiceType="mediaProjection|dataSync" />

        <service
            android:name=".AccessibilityBridge"
            android:permission="android.permission.BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE"
            android:exported="false">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService" />
            </intent-filter>

            <meta-data
                android:name="android.accessibilityservice"
                android:resource="@xml/accessibility_service_config" />
        </service>
    </application>
</manifest>

TV MANIFEST
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    package="com.example.tvremotedesktop">

    <uses-feature android:name="android.software.leanback" android:required="true" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />

    <application
        android:allowBackup="false"
        android:label="TV Client"
        android:supportsRtl="true">

        <activity
            android:name=".MainActivity"
            android:exported="true">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN" />
                <category android:name="android.intent.category.LEANBACK_LAUNCHER" />
            </intent-filter>
        </activity>
    </application>
</manifest>

4) MOBILE APP UI XML
========================================================

========================================================

object ProtocolConstants {
    const val MAGIC = 0x52444D31 // "RDM1"
    const val VERSION = 1

CaptureService.kt
package com.example.mobileremotedesktop

import android.app.*
import android.content.Intent
import android.media.projection.MediaProjection
import android.media.projection.MediaProjectionManager
import android.os.IBinder
import androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat

class CaptureService : Service() {
    private var mediaProjection: MediaProjection? = null
    private var encoder: VideoEncoder? = null
    private var controlServer: ControlServer? = null

    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        startForeground(1, buildNotification("Streaming active"))
        controlServer = ControlServer(applicationContext)
        controlServer?.start()
    }

    override fun onStartCommand(intent: Intent?, flags: Int, startId: Int): Int {
        val resultCode = intent?.getIntExtra("resultCode", Activity.RESULT_CANCELED) ?: Activity.RESULT_CANCELED
        val data = intent?.getParcelableExtra<Intent>("data")
        if (resultCode != Activity.RESULT_CANCELED && data != null) {
            val mpm = getSystemService(MEDIA_PROJECTION_SERVICE) as MediaProjectionManager
            mediaProjection = mpm.getMediaProjection(resultCode, data)
            encoder = VideoEncoder(this, mediaProjection!!) { packet ->
                controlServer?.broadcastVideo(packet)
            }
            encoder?.start()
        }
        return START_STICKY
    }

    override fun onBind(intent: Intent?): IBinder? = null

    override fun onDestroy() {
        encoder?.stop()
        controlServer?.stop()
        mediaProjection?.stop()
        super.onDestroy()
    }

    private fun buildNotification(text: String): Notification {
        val channelId = "stream_channel"
        val nm = getSystemService(NOTIFICATION_SERVICE) as NotificationManager
        if (nm.getNotificationChannel(channelId) == null) {
            nm.createNotificationChannel(NotificationChannel(channelId, "Streaming", NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_LOW))
        }
        return NotificationCompat.Builder(this, channelId)
            .setContentTitle("Mobile Host")
            .setContentText(text)
            .setSmallIcon(android.R.drawable.presence_video_online)
            .build()
    }
}

VideoEncoder.kt
package com.example.mobileremotedesktop

import android.content.Context
import android.media.*
import android.media.projection.MediaProjection
import android.view.Surface
import java.nio.ByteBuffer

class VideoEncoder(
    private val context: Context,
    private val projection: MediaProjection,
    private val onPacket: (ByteArray) -> Unit
) {
    private var codec: MediaCodec? = null
    private var inputSurface: Surface? = null

    fun start() {
        val metrics = context.resources.displayMetrics
        codec = MediaCodec.createEncoderByType("video/avc").apply {
            val format = MediaFormat.createVideoFormat("video/avc", metrics.widthPixels, metrics.heightPixels).apply {
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_FORMAT, MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities.COLOR_FormatSurface)
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_BIT_RATE, 8_000_000)
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_FRAME_RATE, 30)
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_I_FRAME_INTERVAL, 1)
            }
            configure(format, null, null, MediaCodec.CONFIGURE_FLAG_ENCODE)
            inputSurface = createInputSurface()
            start()
        }

        projection.createVirtualDisplay(
            "RDM",
            metrics.widthPixels,
            metrics.heightPixels,
            metrics.densityDpi,
            DisplayManager.VIRTUAL_DISPLAY_FLAG_AUTO_MIRROR,
            inputSurface,
            null,
            null
        )

        Thread {
            val bufferInfo = MediaCodec.BufferInfo()
            while (true) {
                val outIndex = codec?.dequeueOutputBuffer(bufferInfo, 10_000) ?: break
                if (outIndex >= 0) {
                    val buffer = codec!!.getOutputBuffer(outIndex) ?: continue
                    val data = ByteArray(bufferInfo.size)
                    buffer.get(data)
                    buffer.clear()
                    onPacket(data)
                    codec!!.releaseOutputBuffer(outIndex, false)
                }
            }
        }.start()
    }

    fun stop() {
        codec?.stop()
        codec?.release()
        codec = null
    }
}

ControlServer.kt
package com.example.mobileremotedesktop

import android.content.Context
import java.net.ServerSocket
import java.net.Socket
import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList

class ControlServer(private val context: Context) {
    private var serverSocket: ServerSocket? = null
    private val clients = CopyOnWriteArrayList<Socket>()
    private lateinit var inputDispatcher: InputDispatcher

    fun start() {
        inputDispatcher = InputDispatcher(context)
        Thread {
            serverSocket = ServerSocket(5051)
            while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted) {
                val client = serverSocket!!.accept()
                clients.add(client)
                Thread { readLoop(client) }.start()
            }
        }.start()
    }

    private fun readLoop(socket: Socket) {
        val input = socket.getInputStream()
        val buffer = ByteArray(4096)
        while (true) {
            val len = input.read(buffer)
            if (len <= 0) break
            val msg = String(buffer, 0, len)
            inputDispatcher.handle(msg)
        }
    }

    fun broadcastVideo(packet: ByteArray) {
        clients.forEach { client ->
            try {
                client.getOutputStream().write(packet)
                client.getOutputStream().flush()
            } catch (_: Exception) {
            }
        }
    }

    fun stop() {
        try { serverSocket?.close() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        clients.forEach { try { it.close() } catch (_: Exception) {} }
        clients.clear()
    }
}

package com.example.tvremotedesktop

import android.view.SurfaceHolder
import java.net.Socket

class StreamClient(
    private val host: String,
    private val port: Int,
    private val holder: SurfaceHolder,
    private val onStatus: (String) -> Unit
) {
    private var socket: Socket? = null
    private var decoder: VideoDecoder? = null

    fun start() {
        Thread {
            try {
                socket = Socket(host, port)
                onStatus("Status: Receiving")
                decoder = VideoDecoder(holder.surface)
                decoder?.start()
                val input = socket!!.getInputStream()
                val buffer = ByteArray(8192)
                while (true) {
                    val len = input.read(buffer)
                    if (len <= 0) break
                    decoder?.queue(buffer, len)
                }
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                onStatus("Status: Error")
            }
        }.start()
    }

    fun stop() {
        try { socket?.close() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        decoder?.stop()
    }
}

package com.example.tvremotedesktop

import android.media.MediaCodec
import android.media.MediaFormat
import android.view.Surface
import java.nio.ByteBuffer

class VideoDecoder(private val surface: Surface) {
    private var codec: MediaCodec? = null

    fun start() {
        codec = MediaCodec.createDecoderByType("video/avc").apply {
            val format = MediaFormat.createVideoFormat("video/avc", 1920, 1080)
            configure(format, surface, null, 0)
            start()
        }
    }

    fun queue(data: ByteArray, length: Int) {
        val inIndex = codec?.dequeueInputBuffer(10_000) ?: return
        if (inIndex >= 0) {
            val buffer = codec!!.getInputBuffer(inIndex) ?: return
            buffer.clear()
            buffer.put(data, 0, length)
            codec!!.queueInputBuffer(inIndex, 0, length, System.nanoTime() / 1000, 0)
        }
    }

    fun stop() {
        codec?.stop()
        codec?.release()
        codec = null
    }
}

========================================================
9) LOCAL NETWORK COMMUNICATION FLOW
========================================================

Recommended flow:
1. Mobile enables hotspot.
2. TV joins hotspot Wi‑Fi.
3. User opens mobile app and taps Start Hosting.
4. Mobile asks for screen capture consent.
5. Mobile starts foreground capture service.
6. TV enters host IP and connects.
7. TV opens:
   - video socket for stream
   - control socket for input
8. TV decodes and displays video.
9. TV sends remote input events back to mobile.
10. Mobile applies input only in an approved, user-visible manner.

Simple message format for control channel:
- KEY:KEYCODE_DPAD_UP
- KEY:KEYCODE_ENTER
- TEXT:hello
- TAP:120,330

For a real implementation, switch to JSON:
{
  "type":"key",
  "keyCode":23
}

========================================================
10) OPTIMIZATION NOTES
========================================================

For low latency:
- Use MediaCodec with Surface input
- Prefer H.264 for compatibility; H.265 only if both devices support it reliably
- Use 30 FPS or adaptive FPS
- Keyframe interval 1–2 seconds
- Reduce bitrate on weak Wi‑Fi
- Use a single worker thread for encoder output
- Consider UDP for video packets if you implement packet framing and loss handling
- Keep control messages on TCP
- Use partial wake lock on mobile while streaming
- Prefer a fixed resolution or dynamic downscaling if bandwidth drops

About “screen off while still streaming”:
- Android generally restricts hidden/offscreen capture behavior.
- A lawful app should keep a foreground notification visible and follow platform policy.
- If the use case is battery savings, consider dimming the screen or keeping it awake at a low brightness rather than turning it off in a way that bypasses user visibility.

Mobile:
- Media projection consent dialog
- Foreground service notification
- Optional Accessibility Service enabled manually by user in Settings

TV:
- No special permissions required for basic network client use

What I can provide is a safe, legitimate architecture for a consent-based, user-visible remote support / screen-mirroring app pair for Android Mobile + Android TV, focused on:

========================================================
1) HIGH-LEVEL ARCHITECTURE
========================================================

Mobile App (Sender / Host)
- Captures screen using MediaProjection
- Encodes frames with MediaCodec (H.264 or H.265 if supported)
- Streams video packets over local network
- Receives control events from TV client
- Applies input only where permitted:
  - in-app remote control
  - user-approved AccessibilityService for limited actions
- Shows persistent foreground notification while active

TV App (Receiver / Thin Client)
- Connects to mobile host on hotspot/local Wi‑Fi
- Receives stream packets
- Decodes using MediaCodec
- Renders via SurfaceView / TextureView
- Captures TV-side input:
  - DPAD / remote
  - mouse
  - keyboard
- Sends input events back to mobile host

Transport
- TCP for signaling, pairing, control, and keyframes
- UDP for low-latency video packets (optional)
- Fallback to TCP-only for simplicity and reliability

Security
- Pairing code or QR-based session approval
- Session token
- TLS over TCP where feasible
- Signed control messages
- Explicit permission UI on mobile host

package com.example.mobileremotedesktop

import android.app.*
import android.content.Intent
import android.media.projection.MediaProjection
import android.media.projection.MediaProjectionManager
import android.os.IBinder
import androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat

class CaptureService : Service() {
    private var mediaProjection: MediaProjection? = null
    private var encoder: VideoEncoder? = null
    private var controlServer: ControlServer? = null

    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        startForeground(1, buildNotification("Streaming active"))
        controlServer = ControlServer(applicationContext)
        controlServer?.start()
    }

    override fun onStartCommand(intent: Intent?, flags: Int, startId: Int): Int {
        val resultCode = intent?.getIntExtra("resultCode", Activity.RESULT_CANCELED) ?: Activity.RESULT_CANCELED
        val data = intent?.getParcelableExtra<Intent>("data")
        if (resultCode != Activity.RESULT_CANCELED && data != null) {
            val mpm = getSystemService(MEDIA_PROJECTION_SERVICE) as MediaProjectionManager
            mediaProjection = mpm.getMediaProjection(resultCode, data)
            encoder = VideoEncoder(this, mediaProjection!!) { packet ->
                controlServer?.broadcastVideo(packet)
            }
            encoder?.start()
        }
        return START_STICKY
    }

    override fun onBind(intent: Intent?): IBinder? = null

    override fun onDestroy() {
        encoder?.stop()
        controlServer?.stop()
        mediaProjection?.stop()
        super.onDestroy()
    }

    private fun buildNotification(text: String): Notification {
        val channelId = "stream_channel"
        val nm = getSystemService(NOTIFICATION_SERVICE) as NotificationManager
        if (nm.getNotificationChannel(channelId) == null) {
            nm.createNotificationChannel(NotificationChannel(channelId, "Streaming", NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_LOW))
        }
        return NotificationCompat.Builder(this, channelId)
            .setContentTitle("Mobile Host")
            .setContentText(text)
            .setSmallIcon(android.R.drawable.presence_video_online)
            .build()
    }
}

package com.example.mobileremotedesktop

import android.content.Context
import android.media.*
import android.media.projection.MediaProjection
import android.view.Surface
import java.nio.ByteBuffer

class VideoEncoder(
    private val context: Context,
    private val projection: MediaProjection,
    private val onPacket: (ByteArray) -> Unit
) {
    private var codec: MediaCodec? = null
    private var inputSurface: Surface? = null

    fun start() {
        val metrics = context.resources.displayMetrics
        codec = MediaCodec.createEncoderByType("video/avc").apply {
            val format = MediaFormat.createVideoFormat("video/avc", metrics.widthPixels, metrics.heightPixels).apply {
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_FORMAT, MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities.COLOR_FormatSurface)
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_BIT_RATE, 8_000_000)
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_FRAME_RATE, 30)
                setInteger(MediaFormat.KEY_I_FRAME_INTERVAL, 1)
            }
            configure(format, null, null, MediaCodec.CONFIGURE_FLAG_ENCODE)
            inputSurface = createInputSurface()
            start()
        }

        projection.createVirtualDisplay(
            "RDM",
            metrics.widthPixels,
            metrics.heightPixels,
            metrics.densityDpi,
            DisplayManager.VIRTUAL_DISPLAY_FLAG_AUTO_MIRROR,
            inputSurface,
            null,
            null
        )

        Thread {
            val bufferInfo = MediaCodec.BufferInfo()
            while (true) {
                val outIndex = codec?.dequeueOutputBuffer(bufferInfo, 10_000) ?: break
                if (outIndex >= 0) {
                    val buffer = codec!!.getOutputBuffer(outIndex) ?: continue
                    val data = ByteArray(bufferInfo.size)
                    buffer.get(data)
                    buffer.clear()
                    onPacket(data)
                    codec!!.releaseOutputBuffer(outIndex, false)
                }
            }
        }.start()
    }

    fun stop() {
        codec?.stop()
        codec?.release()
        codec = null
    }
}

package com.example.mobileremotedesktop

import android.content.Context
import java.net.ServerSocket
import java.net.Socket
import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList

class ControlServer(private val context: Context) {
    private var serverSocket: ServerSocket? = null
    private val clients = CopyOnWriteArrayList<Socket>()
    private lateinit var inputDispatcher: InputDispatcher

    fun start() {
        inputDispatcher = InputDispatcher(context)
        Thread {
            serverSocket = ServerSocket(5051)
            while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted) {
                val client = serverSocket!!.accept()
                clients.add(client)
                Thread { readLoop(client) }.start()
            }
        }.start()
    }

    private fun readLoop(socket: Socket) {
        val input = socket.getInputStream()
        val buffer = ByteArray(4096)
        while (true) {
            val len = input.read(buffer)
            if (len <= 0) break
            val msg = String(buffer, 0, len)
            inputDispatcher.handle(msg)
        }
    }

    fun broadcastVideo(packet: ByteArray) {
        clients.forEach { client ->
            try {
                client.getOutputStream().write(packet)
                client.getOutputStream().flush()
            } catch (_: Exception) {
            }
        }
    }

    fun stop() {
        try { serverSocket?.close() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        clients.forEach { try { it.close() } catch (_: Exception) {} }
        clients.clear()
    }
}

package com.example.tvremotedesktop

import android.view.SurfaceHolder
import java.net.Socket

class StreamClient(
    private val host: String,
    private val port: Int,
    private val holder: SurfaceHolder,
    private val onStatus: (String) -> Unit
) {
    private var socket: Socket? = null
    private var decoder: VideoDecoder? = null

    fun start() {
        Thread {
            try {
                socket = Socket(host, port)
                onStatus("Status: Receiving")
                decoder = VideoDecoder(holder.surface)
                decoder?.start()
                val input = socket!!.getInputStream()
                val buffer = ByteArray(8192)
                while (true) {
                    val len = input.read(buffer)
                    if (len <= 0) break
                    decoder?.queue(buffer, len)
                }
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                onStatus("Status: Error")
            }
        }.start()
    }

    fun stop() {
        try { socket?.close() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        decoder?.stop()
    }
}

VideoDecoder.kt
package com.example.tvremotedesktop

import android.media.MediaCodec
import android.media.MediaFormat
import android.view.Surface
import java.nio.ByteBuffer

class VideoDecoder(private val surface: Surface) {
    private var codec: MediaCodec? = null

    fun start() {
        codec = MediaCodec.createDecoderByType("video/avc").apply {
            val format = MediaFormat.createVideoFormat("video/avc", 1920, 1080)
            configure(format, surface, null, 0)
            start()
        }
    }

    fun queue(data: ByteArray, length: Int) {
        val inIndex = codec?.dequeueInputBuffer(10_000) ?: return
        if (inIndex >= 0) {
            val buffer = codec!!.getInputBuffer(inIndex) ?: return
            buffer.clear()
            buffer.put(data, 0, length)
            codec!!.queueInputBuffer(inIndex, 0, length, System.nanoTime() / 1000, 0)
        }
    }

    fun stop() {
        codec?.stop()
        codec?.release()
        codec = null
    }
}

========================================================
9) LOCAL NETWORK COMMUNICATION FLOW
========================================================

Recommended flow:
1. Mobile enables hotspot.
2. TV joins hotspot Wi‑Fi.
3. User opens mobile app and taps Start Hosting.
4. Mobile asks for screen capture consent.
5. Mobile starts foreground capture service.
6. TV enters host IP and connects.
7. TV opens:
   - video socket for stream
   - control socket for input
8. TV decodes and displays video.
9. TV sends remote input events back to mobile.
10. Mobile applies input only in an approved, user-visible manner.

Simple message format for control channel:
- KEY:KEYCODE_DPAD_UP
- KEY:KEYCODE_ENTER
- TEXT:hello
- TAP:120,330

For a real implementation, switch to JSON:
{
  "type":"key",
  "keyCode":23
}

========================================================
10) OPTIMIZATION NOTES
========================================================

For low latency:
- Use MediaCodec with Surface input
- Prefer H.264 for compatibility; H.265 only if both devices support it reliably
- Use 30 FPS or adaptive FPS
- Keyframe interval 1–2 seconds
- Reduce bitrate on weak Wi‑Fi
- Use a single worker thread for encoder output
- Consider UDP for video packets if you implement packet framing and loss handling
- Keep control messages on TCP
- Use partial wake lock on mobile while streaming
- Prefer a fixed resolution or dynamic downscaling if bandwidth drops

About “screen off while still streaming”:
- Android generally restricts hidden/offscreen capture behavior.
- A lawful app should keep a foreground notification visible and follow platform policy.
- If the use case is battery savings, consider dimming the screen or keeping it awake at a low brightness rather than turning it off in a way that bypasses user visibility.

========================================================
11) PERMISSIONS AND USER CONSENT
========================================================

Mobile:
- Media projection consent dialog
- Foreground service notification
- Optional Accessibility Service enabled manually by user in Settings

TV:
- No special permissions required for basic network client use

========================================================
12) WHAT TO BUILD NEXT
========================================================

If you want a real production-quality version, the next safe steps are:
- add JSON message framing with length-prefix packets
- add session pairing and authentication
- add ping/latency measurement
- add adaptive bitrate and resolution
- add reconnect logic
- add proper video packetization for MediaCodec output format
- add a visible, user-controlled permissions flow
- add mouse/touch mapping and focus-aware control only within allowed contexts

If you want, I can provide a safe, complete starter template for:
- Kotlin Gradle setup for two Android modules
- length-prefixed TCP protocol
- MediaProjection + MediaCodec boilerplate
- TV SurfaceView decoder pipeline
- JSON control messaging
- pairing PIN workflow

prompt: Lebron Surfers is a fast-paced, endlessly scrolling mobile game presented from a third-person perspective where the camera floats just behind and slightly above a cartoon-styled runner, angled forward so the player can see three parallel train-track lanes stretching endlessly into the distance, with the visual experience drenched in bright, saturated colors and smooth, playful animations designed to feel energetic and youthful; the player character is a stylized, graffiti-inspired teenager with an oversized head, expressive facial features, and rounded proportions, wearing vibrant streetwear such as hoodies, sneakers, hats, and backpacks, with clothing colors that pop sharply against the environment, often using bold reds, yellows, blues, greens, and whites, and every character animation—running, jumping, sliding, stumbling, or activating a power-up—is exaggerated and elastic, with limbs stretching slightly and snapping back to enhance the arcade feel; the environment consists of subway tracks laid on gravel beds with wooden or concrete sleepers, flanked by stationary and moving trains painted in bright primary colors with decals, windows, headlights, and metallic reflections, while the background includes tunnels, platforms, overhead wires, signal lights, fences, billboards, buildings, trees, and city landmarks themed to the current world location, all stylized with clean outlines, soft shading, and minimal texture noise so nothing distracts from gameplay; the ground constantly scrolls forward, giving the illusion of infinite space, while obstacles appear rhythmically in the three lanes, including waist-high barriers with diagonal warning stripes, low ramps, traffic cones, signal boxes, tall trains that block entire lanes, overhead bars that force the player to slide, and ramps that launch the character onto the tops of trains, where additional coin paths and hazards appear; coins are small, flat, glowing gold discs embossed with a simple symbol, outlined with a bright shine, arranged deliberately in straight lines, arcs, zigzags, and stacked vertical patterns that guide player movement, and when collected they emit a sharp metallic chime and a brief sparkle animation that pops outward from the character; power-ups float slightly above the ground and rotate slowly in place, each encased in a glowing outline with distinct colors and icons such as a red-and-white striped magnet icon for coin magnets, green or blue sneakers with upward arrows for super jumps, glowing star or shield icons for invincibility, and hoverboards depicted as colorful boards with decals and glowing edges, which, when activated, trigger dramatic visual effects like screen flashes, particle trails, color shifts, speed lines, and intensified sound effects; the hoverboard snaps instantly under the character’s feet with a mechanical click and glowing streaks, protecting them from one crash while adding sparks and trails as they grind across surfaces; the user interface overlays the gameplay without obstructing vision, placing the score counter at the top center in bold, rounded numerals with a slight bounce animation as numbers increase, the coin counter near the top with a coin icon and bright yellow digits, power-up timers represented by circular icons that drain clockwise, and pause or settings buttons tucked neatly into corners using rounded square icons with clean symbols; menus use large, friendly buttons with thick outlines, soft drop shadows, and bright gradients, often in blues, oranges, and greens, with icons that are instantly readable, such as play arrows, gear symbols, shopping cart icons, and character silhouettes; the main menu shows the character standing idle on the tracks performing looping animations like stretching, bouncing, or playing with their hoverboard while trains roll slowly in the background, and graffiti-style logos with thick outlines, paint drips, and bold typography dominate the top of the screen; the game’s antagonist, a stocky cartoon inspector wearing a uniform and cap, accompanied by a small dog, appears briefly during stumbles or crashes, lunging forward with exaggerated motion and heavy footsteps before the run ends, reinforcing urgency without appearing threatening; audio is constant and layered, featuring upbeat electronic or pop-inspired music with steady rhythm, layered with sound effects such as rhythmic footfalls, coin chimes, swooshing jumps, grinding hoverboards, train horns, collision thuds, and UI clicks, all mixed so nothing overpowers the action; overall, every visual, sound, animation, color, and interface element in Lebron Surfers is meticulously designed to keep the player moving forward, feeling rewarded every few seconds, never overwhelmed by complexity, never punished for long, and always encouraged to try “just one more run,” creating a seamless loop of motion, color, sound, and dopamine that defines the game’s enduring appeal.

FIFA Card Duel

2D Sprite-Based Portrait Only Async Multiplayer Unity / C#

Game Summary

A turn-based football card battler for mobile where players build a 40-card deck, place cards across 5 zones (GK-DEF-MID-ATT-ATT), and resolve attacks with stat-based combat. The design supports asynchronous multiplayer, quick matches, ranked divisions, and draft mode. Monetization is cosmetic-only; energy gates session frequency without pay-to-win benefits.

Turn loop: Draw → Place → Attack → End. Each async turn has a 90-second action window.

Included Deliverables

  • Card.cs
  • GameManager.cs
  • CombatSystem.cs
  • UIManager.cs
  • 50-card JSON database
This response provides a self-contained Unity-oriented implementation blueprint and data set in C# and JSON form.

Card.cs

using System;
using UnityEngine;

public enum CardType
{
    Player,
    Tactic,
    Reaction
}

public enum CardRarity
{
    Bronze = 1,
    Silver = 2,
    Gold = 3,
    Special = 4
}

public enum ZoneType
{
    GK,
    DEF,
    MID,
    ATT1,
    ATT2
}

[Serializable]
public class Card
{
    public string id;
    public string name;
    public CardType type;
    public CardRarity rarity;
    [Range(1, 5)] public int stars = 1;

    // Player stats
    [Range(0, 99)] public int PAC;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int SHO;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int PAS;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int DRI;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int DEF;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int PHY;

    // Meta
    public string club;
    public string nation;
    public string league;
    public string formation; // for Tactic cards, e.g. "4-3-3"
    public string reactionEffect; // for Reaction cards, e.g. "Intercept", "Block", "Counter"
    public string description;
    public Sprite artwork;

    public int ManaCost
    {
        get
        {
            int baseCost = stars + ((int)rarity - 1);
            if (type == CardType.Tactic) baseCost += 1;
            if (type == CardType.Reaction) baseCost += 1;
            return Mathf.Clamp(baseCost, 1, 8);
        }
    }

    public int Overall
    {
        get
        {
            int total = PAC + SHO + PAS + DRI + DEF + PHY;
            return Mathf.RoundToInt(total / 6f);
        }
    }

    public bool IsPlayer => type == CardType.Player;
    public bool IsTactic => type == CardType.Tactic;
    public bool IsReaction => type == CardType.Reaction;

    public string DisplayStatLine()
    {
        return $"PAC {PAC} | SHO {SHO} | PAS {PAS} | DRI {DRI} | DEF {DEF} | PHY {PHY}";
    }

    public Color RarityColor()
    {
        switch (rarity)
        {
            case CardRarity.Bronze: return new Color(0.79f, 0.55f, 0.35f);
            case CardRarity.Silver: return new Color(0.82f, 0.84f, 0.88f);
            case CardRarity.Gold: return new Color(0.95f, 0.76f, 0.31f);
            case CardRarity.Special: return new Color(0.78f, 0.42f, 1f);
            default: return Color.white;
        }
    }

    public static Card Clone(Card c)
    {
        return new Card
        {
            id = c.id,
            name = c.name,
            type = c.type,
            rarity = c.rarity,
            stars = c.stars,
            PAC = c.PAC,
            SHO = c.SHO,
            PAS = c.PAS,
            DRI = c.DRI,
            DEF = c.DEF,
            PHY = c.PHY,
            club = c.club,
            nation = c.nation,
            league = c.league,
            formation = c.formation,
            reactionEffect = c.reactionEffect,
            description = c.description,
            artwork = c.artwork
        };
    }
}

GameManager.cs

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

public enum MatchMode
{
    QuickMatch,
    Ranked,
    Draft
}

public enum TurnPhase
{
    Draw,
    Place,
    Attack,
    End
}

[Serializable]
public class BoardSlot
{
    public ZoneType zone;
    public Card placedCard;
    public bool occupied => placedCard != null;
}

[Serializable]
public class PlayerState
{
    public string playerId;
    public string displayName;
    public int energy = 10;
    public int divisionPoints;
    public int wins;
    public int losses;

    public List<Card> deck = new List<Card>();
    public List<Card> hand = new List<Card>();
    public List<Card> bench = new List<Card>();
    public List<BoardSlot> field = new List<BoardSlot>();

    public int goalsScored;
    public int goalsConceded;
    public int turnTimerSeconds = 90;
    public TurnPhase phase = TurnPhase.Draw;

    public PlayerState(string id, string name)
    {
        playerId = id;
        displayName = name;
        field.Add(new BoardSlot { zone = ZoneType.GK });
        field.Add(new BoardSlot { zone = ZoneType.DEF });
        field.Add(new BoardSlot { zone = ZoneType.MID });
        field.Add(new BoardSlot { zone = ZoneType.ATT1 });
        field.Add(new BoardSlot { zone = ZoneType.ATT2 });
    }
}

public class GameManager : MonoBehaviour
{
    public static GameManager Instance;

    [Header("Match")]
    public MatchMode mode;
    public PlayerState localPlayer;
    public PlayerState remotePlayer;
    public bool isAsyncMultiplayer = true;

    [Header("Timers")]
    public float turnDuration = 90f;
    public float quickMatchDuration = 180f;

    [Header("Deck Rules")]
    public int deckSize = 40;
    public int minPlayers = 11;
    public int benchSize = 5;
    public int maxHandSize = 7;

    [Header("AI")]
    public string aiArchetype = "Balanced"; // Defensive / Balanced / Aggressive

    public event Action<PlayerState> OnStateChanged;
    public event Action<string> OnLog;
    public event Action<PlayerState, Card> OnCardPlaced;
    public event Action<Card, Card, CombatResult> OnCombatResolved;
    public event Action<PlayerState> OnTurnAdvanced;
    public event Action<PlayerState> OnGoalScored;

    private System.Random rng = new System.Random();
    private CombatSystem combatSystem;

    void Awake()
    {
        if (Instance != null && Instance != this) { Destroy(gameObject); return; }
        Instance = this;
        combatSystem = GetComponent<CombatSystem>();
        if (combatSystem == null) combatSystem = gameObject.AddComponent<CombatSystem>();
    }

    public void StartMatch(PlayerState p1, PlayerState p2, MatchMode matchMode)
    {
        localPlayer = p1;
        remotePlayer = p2;
        mode = matchMode;

        SetupDeckAndHand(localPlayer);
        SetupDeckAndHand(remotePlayer);

        localPlayer.phase = TurnPhase.Draw;
        remotePlayer.phase = TurnPhase.Draw;

        Log($"Match started: {p1.displayName} vs {p2.displayName} ({matchMode})");
        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(localPlayer);
        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(remotePlayer);
    }

    void SetupDeckAndHand(PlayerState p)
    {
        Shuffle(p.deck);
        p.hand.Clear();
        p.bench.Clear();

        int initialHand = Mathf.Min(5, p.deck.Count);
        for (int i = 0; i < initialHand; i++)
            DrawCard(p);

        int benchCount = Mathf.Min(benchSize, p.deck.Count);
        for (int i = 0; i < benchCount; i++)
            p.bench.Add(p.deck[i]);
    }

    public void DrawCard(PlayerState p)
    {
        if (p.deck.Count == 0 || p.hand.Count >= maxHandSize) return;
        Card c = p.deck[0];
        p.deck.RemoveAt(0);
        p.hand.Add(c);
        Log($"{p.displayName} draws {c.name}");
        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(p);
    }

    public bool CanPlaceCard(Card c, ZoneType zone)
    {
        if (c == null) return false;
        if (c.type == CardType.Reaction) return false;
        if (c.type == CardType.Tactic) return zone == ZoneType.MID;
        if (c.type == CardType.Player)
        {
            if (zone == ZoneType.GK) return c.DEF >= 55 || c.Overall >= 60;
            if (zone == ZoneType.DEF) return c.DEF >= 45;
            if (zone == ZoneType.MID) return c.PAS + c.DRI >= 85;
            if (zone == ZoneType.ATT1 || zone == ZoneType.ATT2) return c.SHO + c.DRI >= 80;
        }
        return false;
    }

    public bool PlaceCard(PlayerState p, Card c, int zoneIndex)
    {
        if (zoneIndex < 0 || zoneIndex >= p.field.Count) return false;
        BoardSlot slot = p.field[zoneIndex];
        if (slot.occupied) return false;
        if (!p.hand.Contains(c)) return false;
        if (!CanPlaceCard(c, slot.zone)) return false;

        slot.placedCard = c;
        p.hand.Remove(c);
        OnCardPlaced?.Invoke(p, c);
        ApplyChemistry(p);
        Log($"{p.displayName} places {c.name} in {slot.zone}");
        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(p);
        return true;
    }

    void ApplyChemistry(PlayerState p)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < p.field.Count; i++)
        {
            Card current = p.field[i].placedCard;
            if (current == null) continue;

            int boost = 0;
            if (i > 0 && p.field[i - 1].placedCard != null)
            {
                Card left = p.field[i - 1].placedCard;
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(current.club) && current.club == left.club) boost += 1;
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(current.nation) && current.nation == left.nation) boost += 1;
            }
            if (i < p.field.Count - 1 && p.field[i + 1].placedCard != null)
            {
                Card right = p.field[i + 1].placedCard;
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(current.club) && current.club == right.club) boost += 1;
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(current.nation) && current.nation == right.nation) boost += 1;
            }
            if (boost > 0)
            {
                current.PAC = Mathf.Min(99, current.PAC + boost);
                current.SHO = Mathf.Min(99, current.SHO + boost);
                current.PAS = Mathf.Min(99, current.PAS + boost);
                current.DRI = Mathf.Min(99, current.DRI + boost);
                current.DEF = Mathf.Min(99, current.DEF + boost);
                current.PHY = Mathf.Min(99, current.PHY + boost);
            }
        }
    }

    public CombatResult Attack(PlayerState attackerOwner, int attackerZoneIndex, PlayerState defenderOwner, int defenderZoneIndex)
    {
        if (attackerZoneIndex < 0 || attackerZoneIndex >= attackerOwner.field.Count) return CombatResult.Fail("Invalid attacker");
        if (defenderZoneIndex < 0 || defenderZoneIndex >= defenderOwner.field.Count) return CombatResult.Fail("Invalid defender");

        Card attacker = attackerOwner.field[attackerZoneIndex].placedCard;
        Card defender = defenderOwner.field[defenderZoneIndex].placedCard;
        if (attacker == null) return CombatResult.Fail("No attacker card");

        CombatResult result = combatSystem.ResolveAttack(attackerOwner, attacker, defenderOwner, defender, attackerZoneIndex, defenderZoneIndex);

        OnCombatResolved?.Invoke(attacker, defender, result);

        if (result.goal)
        {
            attackerOwner.goalsScored++;
            defenderOwner.goalsConceded++;
            OnGoalScored?.Invoke(attackerOwner);
            Log($"GOAL by {attackerOwner.displayName}!");
        }
        else
        {
            Log(result.message);
        }

        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(attackerOwner);
        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(defenderOwner);
        return result;
    }

    public void EndTurn(PlayerState p)
    {
        p.phase = TurnPhase.End;
        OnTurnAdvanced?.Invoke(p);
        Log($"{p.displayName} ends turn");
        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(p);
    }

    public void AdvanceToNextPhase(PlayerState p)
    {
        p.phase = (TurnPhase)(((int)p.phase + 1) % 4);
        if (p.phase == TurnPhase.Draw) DrawCard(p);
        OnTurnAdvanced?.Invoke(p);
        OnStateChanged?.Invoke(p);
    }

    public void TickAsyncTimer(PlayerState p, float deltaTime)
    {
        p.turnTimerSeconds = Mathf.Max(0, p.turnTimerSeconds - Mathf.RoundToInt(deltaTime));
        if (p.turnTimerSeconds == 0) EndTurn(p);
    }

    public bool IsDeckLegal(PlayerState p)
    {
        if (p.deck == null || p.deck.Count != deckSize) return false;
        int players = 0;
        foreach (var c in p.deck) if (c != null && c.type == CardType.Player) players++;
        return players >= minPlayers;
    }

    public List<Card> BuildDraftPool(List<Card> database, int count)
    {
        List<Card> pool = new List<Card>();
        for (int i = 0; i < count && database.Count > 0; i++)
        {
            int idx = rng.Next(database.Count);
            pool.Add(Card.Clone(database[idx]));
            database.RemoveAt(idx);
        }
        return pool;
    }

    void Shuffle(List<Card> list)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < list.Count; i++)
        {
            int j = rng.Next(i, list.Count);
            (list[i], list[j]) = (list[j], list[i]);
        }
    }

    void Log(string msg)
    {
        Debug.Log(msg);
        OnLog?.Invoke(msg);
    }

    public bool CanPlayEnergy(PlayerState p, int cost) => p.energy >= cost;
    public void SpendEnergy(PlayerState p, int cost) => p.energy = Mathf.Max(0, p.energy - cost);
    public void RegenEnergy(PlayerState p)
    {
        p.energy = Mathf.Min(10, p.energy + 1);
    }
}

CombatSystem.cs

using System;
using UnityEngine;

[Serializable]
public class CombatResult
{
    public bool success;
    public bool goal;
    public int attackerScore;
    public int defenderScore;
    public int damage;
    public string message;

    public static CombatResult Fail(string msg)
    {
        return new CombatResult { success = false, goal = false, message = msg };
    }
}

public class CombatSystem : MonoBehaviour
{
    public CombatResult ResolveAttack(PlayerState attackerOwner, Card attacker, PlayerState defenderOwner, Card defender, int attackerZoneIndex, int defenderZoneIndex)
    {
        int attackStat = GetAttackStat(attacker, attackerZoneIndex);
        int defendStat = defender != null ? GetDefendStat(defender, defenderZoneIndex) : GetEmptyLaneDefense(defenderZoneIndex);

        int tacticBonusA = GetTacticBonus(attackerOwner, attackerZoneIndex);
        int tacticBonusD = GetTacticBonus(defenderOwner, defenderZoneIndex);

        int reactionBonusD = GetReactionBonus(defenderOwner, defenderZoneIndex);

        int attackerScore = attackStat + tacticBonusA + UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, 6);
        int defenderScore = defendStat + tacticBonusD + reactionBonusD + UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, 6);

        bool beat = attackerScore > defenderScore;
        bool isGoal = beat && defenderZoneIndex == 0;

        string msg;
        if (isGoal) msg = $"{attacker.name} beats GK and scores!";
        else if (beat) msg = $"{attacker.name} wins the duel.";
        else msg = defender != null ? $"{defender.name} stops {attacker.name}." : "Attack contained.";

        return new CombatResult
        {
            success = true,
            goal = isGoal,
            attackerScore = attackerScore,
            defenderScore = defenderScore,
            damage = beat ? 1 : 0,
            message = msg
        };
    }

    int GetAttackStat(Card c, int zoneIndex)
    {
        if (c == null) return 0;
        if (zoneIndex == 0) return c.PAS + c.PHY;
        if (zoneIndex == 1) return c.DEF + c.PHY;
        if (zoneIndex == 2) return c.PAS + c.DRI;
        return c.SHO + c.DRI + c.PAC / 2;
    }

    int GetDefendStat(Card c, int zoneIndex)
    {
        if (c == null) return 0;
        if (zoneIndex == 0) return c.DEF + c.PHY + 10;
        if (zoneIndex == 1) return c.DEF + c.PHY;
        if (zoneIndex == 2) return c.PAS + c.DEF;
        return c.DEF + c.PHY / 2;
    }

    int GetEmptyLaneDefense(int zoneIndex)
    {
        switch (zoneIndex)
        {
            case 0: return 35;
            case 1: return 25;
            case 2: return 20;
            default: return 15;
        }
    }

    int GetTacticBonus(PlayerState p, int zoneIndex)
    {
        int bonus = 0;
        foreach (var slot in p.field)
        {
            if (slot.placedCard != null && slot.placedCard.type == CardType.Tactic)
            {
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(slot.placedCard.formation))
                {
                    if (slot.placedCard.formation == "4-3-3" && zoneIndex >= 2) bonus += 2;
                    if (slot.placedCard.formation == "5-4-1" && zoneIndex <= 1) bonus += 2;
                    if (slot.placedCard.formation == "4-2-3-1" && zoneIndex == 2) bonus += 2;
                }
            }
        }
        return bonus;
    }

    int GetReactionBonus(PlayerState p, int zoneIndex)
    {
        int bonus = 0;
        foreach (var slot in p.field)
        {
            if (slot.placedCard != null && slot.placedCard.type == CardType.Reaction)
            {
                if (slot.placedCard.reactionEffect == "Intercept" && zoneIndex == 2) bonus += 3;
                if (slot.placedCard.reactionEffect == "Block" && zoneIndex <= 1) bonus += 3;
                if (slot.placedCard.reactionEffect == "Counter" && zoneIndex == 0) bonus += 2;
            }
        }
        return bonus;
    }
}

using System.Collections.Generic;

public class UIManager : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Header("Top Stats")]
    public TextMeshProUGUI scoreText;
    public TextMeshProUGUI turnText;
    public TextMeshProUGUI energyText;
    public TextMeshProUGUI timerText;

    [Header("Field")]
    public Transform fieldRoot;
    public List<Button> zoneButtons = new List<Button>();

    [Header("Hand")]
    public Transform handRoot;
    public GameObject handCardPrefab;
    public ScrollRect handScroll;

    [Header("Card Zoom")]
    public GameObject zoomPanel;
    public TextMeshProUGUI zoomName;
    public TextMeshProUGUI zoomStats;
    public TextMeshProUGUI zoomDesc;
    public Image zoomBorder;
    public Button closeZoomButton;

    private GameManager gm;
    private Card selectedCard;
    private int selectedZone = -1;

    void Start()
    {
        gm = GameManager.Instance;
        if (gm != null)
        {
            gm.OnStateChanged += Refresh;
            gm.OnLog += _ => Refresh(gm.localPlayer);
            gm.OnCardPlaced += OnCardPlaced;
            gm.OnGoalScored += _ => Refresh(gm.localPlayer);
        }

        if (closeZoomButton != null) closeZoomButton.onClick.AddListener(HideZoom);
        HideZoom();
    }

    void OnDestroy()
    {
        if (gm != null)
        {
            gm.OnStateChanged -= Refresh;
            gm.OnGoalScored -= _ => Refresh(gm.localPlayer);
        }
    }

    public void Refresh(PlayerState p)
    {
        if (gm == null || p == null) return;

        scoreText.text = $"{gm.localPlayer.goalsScored} - {gm.remotePlayer.goalsScored}";
        turnText.text = $"{p.displayName} • {p.phase}";
        energyText.text = $"Energy {p.energy}/10";
        timerText.text = $"{p.turnTimerSeconds}s";

        RebuildHand();
        UpdateField();
    }

    void RebuildHand()
    {
        if (gm == null || gm.localPlayer == null) return;

        for (int i = handRoot.childCount - 1; i >= 0; i--) Destroy(handRoot.GetChild(i).gameObject);

        foreach (Card c in gm.localPlayer.hand)
        {
            GameObject go = Instantiate(handCardPrefab, handRoot);
            CardView view = go.GetComponent<CardView>();
            if (view != null) view.Bind(c, OnTapCard, OnDragCard);
        }
    }

    void UpdateField()
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < zoneButtons.Count && i < gm.localPlayer.field.Count; i++)
        {
            int idx = i;
            zoneButtons[i].onClick.RemoveAllListeners();
            zoneButtons[i].onClick.AddListener(() => OnZoneTapped(idx));
        }
    }

    void OnTapCard(Card c)
    {
        selectedCard = c;
        ShowZoom(c);
    }

    void OnDragCard(Card c)
    {
        selectedCard = c;
    }

    void OnZoneTapped(int idx)
    {
        selectedZone = idx;
        if (selectedCard != null)
        {
            if (gm.PlaceCard(gm.localPlayer, selectedCard, idx))
            {
                selectedCard = null;
                selectedZone = -1;
                HideZoom();
            }
        }
    }

    public void OnAttackButton()
    {
        if (selectedZone < 0) return;
        gm.Attack(gm.localPlayer, selectedZone, gm.remotePlayer, selectedZone);
    }

    void ShowZoom(Card c)
    {
        if (zoomPanel == null || c == null) return;
        zoomPanel.SetActive(true);
        zoomName.text = c.name;
        zoomStats.text = c.DisplayStatLine();
        zoomDesc.text = $"{c.description}\n\nClub: {c.club}\nNation: {c.nation}\nRarity: {c.rarity} • {c.stars}★";
        if (zoomBorder != null) zoomBorder.color = c.RarityColor();
    }

    void HideZoom()
    {
        if (zoomPanel != null) zoomPanel.SetActive(false);
    }

    void OnCardPlaced(PlayerState p, Card c)
    {
        if (p == gm.localPlayer) Refresh(p);
    }
}

public class CardView : MonoBehaviour
{
    public TextMeshProUGUI title;
    public TextMeshProUGUI statLine;
    public Image rarityFrame;
    private Card boundCard;
    private System.Action<Card> tapCallback;
    private System.Action<Card> dragCallback;

    public void Bind(Card c, System.Action<Card> onTap, System.Action<Card> onDrag)
    {
        boundCard = c;
        tapCallback = onTap;
        dragCallback = onDrag;
        if (title != null) title.text = c.name;
        if (statLine != null) statLine.text = c.type == CardType.Player ? c.DisplayStatLine() : c.description;
        if (rarityFrame != null) rarityFrame.color = c.RarityColor();
    }

    public void OnTap() { tapCallback?.Invoke(boundCard); }
    public void OnDragStart() { dragCallback?.Invoke(boundCard); }
}

FIFA Card Duel

2D Sprite-Based Portrait Only Async Multiplayer Unity / C#

Game Summary

A turn-based football card battler for mobile where players build a 40-card deck, place cards across 5 zones (GK-DEF-MID-ATT-ATT), and resolve attacks with stat-based combat. The design supports asynchronous multiplayer, quick matches, ranked divisions, and draft mode. Monetization is cosmetic-only; energy gates session frequency without pay-to-win benefits.

Turn loop: Draw → Place → Attack → End. Each async turn has a 90-second action window.

Included Deliverables

  • Card.cs
  • GameManager.cs
  • CombatSystem.cs
  • UIManager.cs
  • 50-card JSON database
This response provides a self-contained Unity-oriented implementation blueprint and data set in C# and JSON form.

Card.cs

using System;
using UnityEngine;

public enum CardType
{
    Player,
    Tactic,
    Reaction
}

public enum CardRarity
{
    Bronze = 1,
    Silver = 2,
    Gold = 3,
    Special = 4
}

public enum ZoneType
{
    GK,
    DEF,
    MID,
    ATT1,
    ATT2
}

[Serializable]
public class Card
{
    public string id;
    public string name;
    public CardType type;
    public CardRarity rarity;
    [Range(1, 5)] public int stars = 1;

    // Player stats
    [Range(0, 99)] public int PAC;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int SHO;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int PAS;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int DRI;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int DEF;
    [Range(0, 99)] public int PHY;

    // Meta
    public string club;
    public string nation;
    public string league;
    public string formation; // for Tactic cards, e.g. "4-3-3"
    public string reactionEffect; // for Reaction cards, e.g. "Intercept", "Block", "Counter"
    public string description;
    public Sprite artwork;

    public int ManaCost
    {
        get
        {
            int baseCost = stars + ((int)rarity - 1);
            if (type == CardType.Tactic) baseCost += 1;
            if (type == CardType.Reaction) baseCost += 1;
            return Mathf.Clamp(baseCost, 1, 8);
        }
    }

    public int Overall
    {
        get
        {
            int total = PAC + SHO + PAS + DRI + DEF + PHY;
            return Mathf.RoundToInt(total / 6f);
        }
    }

    public bool IsPlayer => type == CardType.Player;
    public bool IsTactic => type == CardType.Tactic;
    public bool IsReaction => type == CardType.Reaction;

    public string DisplayStatLine()
    {
        return $"PAC {PAC} | SHO {SHO} | PAS {PAS} | DRI {DRI} | DEF {DEF} | PHY {PHY}";
    }

    public Color RarityColor()
    {
        switch (rarity)
        {
            case CardRarity.Bronze: return new Color(0.79f, 0.55f, 0.35f);
            case CardRarity.Silver: return new Color(0.82f, 0.84f, 0.88f);
            case CardRarity.Gold: return new Color(0.95f, 0.76f, 0.31f);
            case CardRarity.Special: return new Color(0.78f, 0.42f, 1f);
            default: return Color.white;
        }
    }

    public static Card Clone(Card c)
    {
        return new Card
        {
            id = c.id,
            name = c.name,
            type = c.type,
            rarity = c.rarity,
            stars = c.stars,
            PAC = c.PAC,
            SHO = c.SHO,
            PAS = c.PAS,
            DRI = c.DRI,
            DEF = c.DEF,
            PHY = c.PHY,
            club = c.club,
            nation = c.nation,
            league = c.league,
            formation = c.formation,
            reactionEffect = c.reactionEffect,
            description = c.description,
            artwork = c.artwork
        };
    }
}
